name: Matrix Multiplication
html:
Ah friend, welcome back! In the previous question we gave you a demonstration of 2-D arrays and in this question we are going to learn to apply it. You didn't think that we would let you off you so easily, did you?

Important Links: Question video, Solution video

Watch video

Have you given the question a thorough read? Did you realize that you have already studied this question in Mathematics? If you don't remember, let us help you jog your memory.

Problem Discussion:

Reader, this question takes 2 matrices as the input and returns the product of those matrices on multiplication. Here, n1=no. of rows and m1=no. of columns of the First Matrix. And, n2=no. of rows and m2=no.of columns of the Second Matrix.

You must understand that all matrices can't be multiplied with each other. Only if m1=n2, then a product matrix can be formed of size n1*m2.

Let's understand this through an example:

You are given a matrix A[2][3] and another matrix B[3][4]. Do you think these 2 matrices can be multiplied with each other? YES! As m1=n2=3, so a new matrix, say P is formed of size n1*m2 i.e. P[2][4] as shown below.

You can also watch the question video if you still have any doubts.

Watch video Approach:

Next we need to understand how to calculate the elements in the product matrix P. For that look at the formula below:

By the above statement, the value at p01 is the sum of the product of elements at the 0th row of the 1st matrix with the elements at the 1st column of the 2nd matrix.

Reader, notice in the formula that in the array "a", the row remains the same each time and column changes and in the array "b", the column remains the same each time and the row changes.

By the formula in figure 2, the marked cell in figure 3 can be represented as:

Similarly, all the other elements of the matrix can be calculated.

We suggest you to write a pseudo code based on all the information you have taken in till now. It'll help you in getting a clear image of the problem at hand.

Refer to the following code and simultaneously view the explanation under it:

import java.io.*; import java.util.*; public class matrixMultiply { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { Scanner scn = new Scanner(System.in); int n1 = scn.nextInt(); int m1 = scn.nextInt(); int[][] arr1 = new int[n1][m1]; for (int i = 0; i < n1; i++) { //1 for (int j = 0; j < m1; j++) { arr1[i][j] = scn.nextInt(); } } int n2 = scn.nextInt(); int m2 = scn.nextInt(); int[][] arr2 = new int[n2][m2]; for (int i = 0; i < n2; i++) { //2 for (int j = 0; j < m2; j++) { arr2[i][j] = scn.nextInt(); } } if (m1 != n2) { System.out.print("Invalid input"); //3 return; } int[][] ans = new int[n1][m2]; for (int i = 0; i < n1; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < m2; j++) { //4 for (int k = 0; k < m1; k++) { ans[i][j] += (arr1[i][k] * arr2[k][j]); } } } for (int i = 0; i < n1; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < m2; j++) { System.out.print(ans[i][j] + " "); //5 } System.out.println(); } } }
java; true"; Analysis

Reader, let us now explain the above code. We are sure it'll be a child's play for you.

  1. We take the input of the number of rows and columns followed by the elements of the first matrix . We have already discussed how to do that in the previous question of 2D Arrays Demo. Watch video
  2. Similarly we take another input of the number of rows and columns followed by the elements of the second matrix.
  3. We check whether it is possible to multiply the 2 matrices (as already discussed in the "WHAT" section) . If the condition is satisfied we print "Invalid Input" and terminate the program else we move forward.
  4. The product array is filled here .For ans[i][j] , we add the new product with fixed "i" and "j" and change "k" to the ans[i][j].
    We highly suggest you refer to the Youtube video Matrix Multiplication [6:38 -8:51] for a deep and thorough explanation of this code snippet. Watch video
  5. At last reader, we print the output of the product matrix as we have already learnt in the previous question.
Time Complexity:

O(n3)

This time complexity is cubic because 3 nested for loops are used.

SPACE COMPLEXITY:

O(n2)

As 2D arrays are used to store numbers, therefore space complexity is quadratic.

With this, we come to the end of this question. Revise this question multiple times as any new concept needs time to settle in our minds. Don't lose hope if you don't crack the question in the first try, nobody does!
